evidence.quote: Some existing methods leverage depth information from an off-the-shelf depth estimator to assist 3D detection, but suffer from the additional computational burden and achieve limited performance caused by inaccurate depth priors.
Previous methods have achieved superior performance based on the accurate depth information from multiple sensors, such as LiDAR signal [18,24,41,42] or stereo matching [7, 25, 46, 54].

solution.approach: To alleviate this, we propose MonoDTR, a novel end-to-end depth-aware transformer network for monocular 3D object detection.

evidence.quote: To alleviate this, we propose MonoDTR, a novel end-to-end depth-aware transformer network for monocular 3D object detection.
Moreover, different from conventional pixel-wise positional encodings, we introduce a novel depth positional encoding (DPE) to inject depth positional hints into transformers.
To address the above issues, we propose MonoDTR, a novel end-to-end depth-aware transformer network for monocular 3D object detection (see Figure 1(c)).

items: Some existing methods leverage depth information from an off-the-shelf depth estimator to assist 3D detection, but suffer from the additional computational burden and achieve limited performance caused by inaccurate depth priors.
However, the performance is still far from satisfactory without the aid of depth cues.
These methods, though better localize objects with the help of estimated depth, may suffer from the risk of learning 3D detection on inaccurate depth maps.
However, the above purely monocular methods fail to accurately localize objects due to the lack of depth cues.
